issues.legal_issue: A later compromise that allocates property jointly to a parent and child can establish their rights between themselves despite an earlier partition among the family members.
material_facts: An earlier partition among the five brothers was found and was not challenged.
In a later suit, a compromise provided for the family lands to be divided into five shares, with three shares allocated jointly to a father and his minor natural son.
The compromise did not separately define the father’s and son’s interests in the three shares.
The son was adopted by another brother, and his widow claimed a share in the properties.
issues.conclusion: The father and son took the properties allocated to them under the compromise jointly, and their rights between themselves flowed from that compromise notwithstanding the earlier partition. The son’s widow could not be denied a share in those properties.
issues.legal_principle: Where a compromise allocates property jointly to a parent and a minor child without separately defining their interests, their rights between themselves arise under the compromise. The judgment relies on no statutory provision or earlier case.

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: A party appealed in a suit seeking partition of family property.
predicates.earlier_family_partition: The family members had previously divided family property among themselves.
predicates.later_compromise_allocated_property_join: The parties later entered a compromise allocating property jointly to a parent and child.
predicates.compromise_did_not_separately_define_the: The compromise did not specify the parent’s and child’s separate interests in the jointly allocated property.

issues.definition: When a partition appeal concerns property allocated jointly to a parent and child by a later compromise that does not define their separate interests, the child or the child’s successor is entitled to a share in that property.

issues.legal_issue: Property acquired in one family member’s name may be treated as acquired from joint-family property income when the family member and another member held property jointly and there is no evidence of a separate source of income.
material_facts: The father and son held the properties allocated to them under the compromise jointly.
Some properties claimed in the suit had later been acquired in the father’s name.
There was no indication that the father had separate income from which to acquire those properties, and the evidence was sparse.
The son’s widow sought a share in the properties.
issues.conclusion: In the circumstances, the later-acquired properties were presumed to have been acquired with income from the jointly held properties, so the widow could claim a share in them.
issues.legal_principle: In the circumstances of sparse evidence, where property is jointly held and there is no indication of a separate income source for the member in whose name later property was acquired, the acquisition may be presumed to have been made with income from the joint property. The judgment relies on no statutory provision or earlier case.

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: A party appealed in a suit seeking partition of family property.
predicates.later_property_acquired_in_one_members_n: Additional property was later acquired in the name of one of those family members.
predicates.no_evidence_of_that_members_separate_inc: There was no evidence that the acquiring family member had a separate source of income for the acquisition.

issues.definition: When a partition appeal concerns later property acquired in one family member’s name, and the family members held property jointly with no evidence of that member’s separate income, the later property is treated as acquired from income of the jointly held property.
